transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, doctor, I guess I'm here because... I just don't care about anything anymore. I've completely stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. I used to go to salsa nights, church gatherings, you know, I'd even cook for the neighbors sometimes. Now, I don't want to do any of it. I'm a carpenter, and I used to love just walking into my shop to smell the wood. But lately... I don't even care about that. It's just all gone.
How long have you been feeling this way? When did you first notice these changes?

It's been about two months now. I first noticed it right after my wife's health took a sudden turn for the worse. Our whole daily routine changed, and... yeah, that's when this whole shift in my mood really started.
Have you noticed any changes in your energy levels or do you feel more tired than usual lately?

Yeah, I have. I'm just exhausted all the time. Even after sitting down for a while, or... or getting a full night in bed, my body just feels completely worn out. It feels exactly like I've been framing a roof all day, even when I haven't done much of anything. Just doing small chores, like trying to load my tools into the truck... it just feels like it's too much right now.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, I do. Pretty much all day, every day. Most mornings I wake up and... there's just this heavy, empty feeling right in my chest. It's like all the color has just gone out of the house. I spend a lot of the day just trying to hold it together. I have to really force myself not to break down in front of my wife.
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to focus, make decisions, or think clearly lately?

Yeah, I have. It's... it's been pretty frustrating, honestly. I'll be at work and I'll stare at blueprints I've been reading my whole life, and the lines just kind of blur together in my head. I just can't seem to process them. It's gotten to the point where I end up asking the younger guys on the crew to repeat things that I really should understand right away. My head just feels too cloudy to think straight.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or on the flip side, feeling restless or fidgety lately?

Yeah, the guys at work have actually pointed it out. Some days it's like... like my boots are full of wet cement. It takes me forever just to walk across the site or pick up a piece of lumber. I just move so slow. But then other times, I'm the complete opposite. I get this restless feeling and I'll just pace around the shop, rubbing my hands together, not actually getting any real work done. It's just one extreme or the other.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently?

No, I haven't really noticed any changes there. I mean... I still eat about the same. My wife packs my lunch for the site, and I usually get through it. I haven't stepped on a scale lately or anything, but my work pants fit the same as they always do. So, no, my appetite and weight seem pretty much normal.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty about things you've done or maybe feeling like you're not worth much lately?

Yeah, I have. A lot, actually. I... I keep thinking about my wife's health. She's been having some issues, and I just keep replaying every single doctor's appointment, every little change in how she's been doing. I just keep telling myself that if I was a better husband, I would have caught it sooner, you know? Like I should have been able to protect her from it somehow. It just feels like I've really let her down.
Have you found yourself thinking about death or dying, or wishing you were dead?

Yeah, I have. I mean, I wouldn't say I'm making a plan or anything, but... I've definitely had thoughts that maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. It's just so heavy sometimes. And, honestly, sometimes I catch myself thinking that my wife and the kids might just be better off without me around to drag them down. It scares me when I think like that, but... those thoughts are definitely there.
Can you describe for me exactly how slow or restless you feel? Are these changes noticeable to other people, like the guys at work or your family?

Yeah, they've noticed. The guys on the crew, I mean. 

It kind of goes two ways. Sometimes I just... I move like my work boots are full of wet cement. It'll take me forever just to bend over and pick up a single board. But then other times, I get this restless feeling. I'll just get stuck pacing around the shop, rubbing my hands together, and I'm not actually getting anything useful done. So, yeah, it's definitely noticeable to the people I work with.
Can you tell me more about how slow you feel when you're moving? Does it take much longer than usual to complete tasks because of this slowness?

Well, it's just... everything feels heavier, like I said. I wouldn't say it's taking me that much longer to finish a job, really. I mean, I still get the work done, eventually. It's just that the physical act of doing it—lifting the hammer, measuring a cut—it just feels like it takes so much more effort than it used to. But as far as the actual time it takes to finish a task... I'm not really sure if it's taking me longer or if it just feels that way. I haven't really timed myself or anything.
How often do you feel slowed down or restless—does it happen every day, and does it last for most of the day?

I'm honestly not sure. I haven't really been keeping track of it like that. I mean, it happens enough that the guys at the shop notice, but... is it every single day? I don't know. And as for how long it lasts when it happens... I couldn't really tell you if it's most of the day or just parts of it. I just know it's been happening a lot lately, but I don't really have an exact timeline for you.
Have you completely lost interest or pleasure in all activities, including things that you used to enjoy like carpentry or spending time with your wife?

Yeah, I have. That's actually the main thing that brings me in, to be honest. I've just... I've stopped wanting to do the things that usually keep me going. 

We used to do salsa nights, go to church gatherings, cook for the neighbors... but I just don't have any interest in any of that right now. I don't even want to walk into my shop just to enjoy the smell of the wood anymore. The drive to do any of those things is just completely gone.
Can you tell me specifically if there’s any activity, even something small, that you still take pleasure in or look forward to doing?

No, not really. Like I was just saying, that's exactly why I'm here. I've completely stopped wanting to do the things that used to keep me going. I don't look forward to salsa nights with my wife, or church gatherings, or cooking for the neighbors anymore. I don't even have the desire to just walk into my shop and smell the wood. There isn't really anything, big or small, that I still enjoy right now.
Just to be clear, have these symptoms been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

I really couldn't tell you the exact timeline. Like I mentioned earlier, I haven't been keeping track of it day by day like that. It definitely feels like it's been going on for a while, but... whether it's been exactly two weeks, or if it's every single day for most of the day... I honestly don't know for sure. I just know I've been stuck in this rut lately and I can't seem to shake it.
